# Verification analysis: redundant-path-failover-ubuntu16

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent transit networks, and each
> serves a private network with one host on it, `node3` and `node4`. Carry
> traffic between the two private networks so the hosts keep reaching each
> other when either transit network is taken out of service, and show that
> continuing across one such transition.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 ubuntu16.04**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit-a, transit-b, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `redundant-path-failover-ubuntu16__3y4caFx`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built OSPF-based ECMP routing over both transit links between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) and directly demonstrated, twice, that node3<->node4 connectivity survives a bounded outage of either transit network with near-zero packet loss and automatic OSPF reconvergence, followed by full restoration on link return. All four nodes were also carried through the mandated one-at-a-time restart protocol with matching pre/post boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots) and confirmed post-restart recovery of routing and end-to-end reachability. A real rp_filter bug surfaced during the node1 restart cycle was root-caused with tcpdump and fixed rather than worked around blindly.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 116/13 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Establish dual redundant transit paths (two /30 links) between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) carrying dynamic routing so traffic can be carried across either path
  - **Why:** Both transit subnets (10.10.1.0/30, 10.10.2.0/30) were addressed on node1/node2 and confirmed reachable (cmd-80ba2c9137584f67, cmd-c5ea9a8f0ee144d8). OSPF area 0.0.0.0 was configured natively on VyOS FRR and via os-frr/Quagga on OPNsense, with Full adjacency formed on both transit links from both routers and an ECMP route to the far private subnet installed via both next-hops (cmd-8bb68c98c840420e, cmd-94f10db9f19d4abe, cmd-62f03553e32f4f15, cmd-b92df274d0474c25).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-53d217bb18e34d64`, `cmd-a6b4c10d31ca40d2`, `cmd-80ba2c9137584f67`, `cmd-c5ea9a8f0ee144d8`, `cmd-4ebe4f1ba99a4adb`, `cmd-e2eeb446a9ba4d1e`, `cmd-8bb68c98c840420e`, `cmd-94f10db9f19d4abe`, `cmd-62f03553e32f4f15`, `cmd-b92df274d0474c25`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Private hosts node3 (behind node1) and node4 (behind node2) reach each other end-to-end across the transit fabric
  - **Why:** Direct pings from node3 (10.10.10.10) to node4 (10.10.20.10) and vice versa succeeded with 0% loss after addressing and OSPF convergence.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f05de919370d40b0`, `cmd-efe5c769072742f3`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Connectivity between node3 and node4 continues when transit network A is taken out of service, and is restored when it returns
  - **Why:** A continuous ping (0.3s interval) from node3 to node4 was running when VyOS eth1 (transit-A) was administratively disabled; log analysis showed zero gaps across all 66 then 117 continuous sequence numbers spanning the disable/re-enable transition, and OSPF neighbor/route state directly confirmed adjacency dropped to transit-B-only during the outage and returned to dual Full adjacency after restoration.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9f18d610201a4cc8`, `cmd-8edb08eb2c91472d`, `cmd-86b690b6064749f9`, `cmd-26537e9d88ae4536`, `cmd-aaa3c3a865fa4e4d`, `cmd-a2362fe0f9ea4ff2`, `cmd-d68d67872d514487`, `cmd-3b9ca242aeb74da4`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Connectivity between node3 and node4 continues when transit network B is taken out of service, and is restored when it returns
  - **Why:** A second continuous ping was running when OPNsense vtnet2 (transit-B) was taken down and later restored; only 1 packet was lost out of 147, with OSPF neighbor/route state directly showing reconvergence to transit-A alone during the outage and full dual-path adjacency restored afterward, demonstrating the required failover transition a second time on the other link.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b0886a415aa74455`, `cmd-a7458d4d596a4799`, `cmd-1c9c33ebc3c24f88`, `cmd-6932d91e9ee84182`, `cmd-0fcc4d317576485b`, `cmd-9ea2476ff1364453`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4): pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
  - **Why:** Each node had a pre-restart boot identity captured (node1 boot_id 7668189d, node2 kern.boottime 06:25:39, node3 boot_id 6ab98831, node4 boot_id 225ffbf7), a native restart issued with acknowledgement (return before disconnect / connection-refused polling confirming downtime), a changed post-restart boot identity (91db428f, 06:40:28, f8a76314, f6fb5627 respectively, all corroborated by the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot), and recovered interface/routing/reachability state confirmed per node plus a final full-topology check showing Full OSPF adjacency on both transit links and successful node3<->node4 ping after all four restarts.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-30a66b0a86a1407d`, `cmd-56ddf8ed33cd4245`, `cmd-a11eacf5ebc8439a`, `cmd-8cea631e8eab4884`, `cmd-278532f78df84a8d`, `cmd-9eac8b35e93142fd`, `cmd-f00d2998024f4c3a`, `cmd-ff27cd249cc6485d`, `cmd-4d00d4775c934b8f`, `cmd-432f18c1c6884fa3`, `cmd-62b40151f7c9443a`, `cmd-7044fd524d454915`, `cmd-19c3950f151b4021`, `cmd-9de40b685c9540e2`, `cmd-5e9229e5026e4760`, `cmd-70e240012ed4442b`, `cmd-50caa05b7b3146de`, `cmd-7edebcca8cc2469e`, `cmd-99082d12808e46f9`, `cmd-898a05942fc54ce9`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to task outcomes: interface/OSPF/firewall configuration on node1/node2, IP/route/sysctl configuration on node3/node4, the four restarts, and the bounded ping/tcpdump diagnostics used to root-cause the rp_filter issue (tcpdump processes were explicitly killed with pkill/kill after use, e.g. cmd-cce23dda3158476e, cmd-f5f4cf6e693a4d02). The rp_filter sysctl change on node3/node4 (cmd-bb06065e87024a12, cmd-8b716b75b0ac4be4, cmd-5cfb2d18d18e4154) is a real, low-risk, narrowly-scoped fix persisted to /etc/sysctl.conf that was directly required to make ECMP-routed replies work, not an unrelated experiment. Minor residue: helper python scripts (/tmp/f.py, /tmp/f2.py, /tmp/f3.py on node2) and continuous-ping log files (/tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping2.log on node3) were left in /tmp rather than explicitly removed, though these are low-risk and likely cleared by the subsequent reboots of both nodes.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-771d7cee7713415c`, `cmd-9d693908c00c483d`, `cmd-474c18ef47384b8f`, `cmd-9f18d610201a4cc8`, `cmd-b0886a415aa74455`, `cmd-bb06065e87024a12`, `cmd-5cfb2d18d18e4154`

### Comments and limitations

- Node1's own post-restart OSPF/reachability recovery was not immediately clean — one neighbor briefly showed 2-Way/DROther and node1->node4 pings failed repeatedly until the rp_filter issue on node3/node4 was diagnosed and fixed; final state was confirmed healthy but the trace shows an extended troubleshooting period rather than an immediately smooth recovery.
- Minor temp-file residue (python config scripts on node2, ping-log files on node3) was not explicitly cleaned up, though low-risk and likely cleared by subsequent reboots.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
